mainTopic: A quoted משנה about a סאה of impure תרומה that fell into one hundred סאה of pure חולין: does it get nullified, and how must the mixture be eaten?
overview: The גמרא is quoting a משנה about one סאה of impure תרומה that fell into one hundred סאה of pure חולין. רבי אליעזר says one סאה is lifted out and left to rot. He reasons that we view it as the very same impure סאה that fell in. The חכמים say the תרומה is nullified in the hundred, so nothing has to rot. Even so, the impure תרומה is still mixed in, so they require the food to be kept from becoming able to receive טומאה. It may be eaten dry or roasted, or kneaded with fruit juice. It may also be split into small doughs with less than a כביצה of the תרומה in each. The amud ends as the גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא about "those חולין", and that ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: Lift out one סאה and let it rot
steps.stepSummary: In the quoted משנה, רבי אליעזר rules that one סאה is removed from the mixture and left to rot as impure תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If a סאה of impure תרומה fell] into one hundred סאה of pure חולין, רבי אליעזר says: one סאה is lifted out and left to rot. I say that the סאה that fell in is the same סאה that came out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of quoting a משנה. Here we hear רבי אליעזר's view on impure תרומה that fell into a mixture of pure חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the סאה you take out of such a mixture is eaten as pure תרומה by a כהן. רבי אליעזר treats the removed סאה as if it were the very same impure סאה that fell in. Impure תרומה cannot be eaten, so this סאה must be left to rot. The rest of the mixture stays pure חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: A unit of volume (a measure of produce)
It is lifted out (separated as תרומה)
It is left to rot (it may not be eaten)
"For I say": a legal assumption: we view the case as if this is what happened (here, that the removed סאה is the one that fell in)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר does not say the mixture is forbidden. Only the one סאה that is removed has to rot. The rest is fine as חולין.

phrases.english: into one hundred [se'a] of pure non-sacred produce,
phrases.notes: The start of this case comes just before: a סאה of impure תרומה fell in.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: let it be lifted out and left to rot,

phrases.aramaic: הִיא סְאָה שֶׁנָּפְלָה הִיא סְאָה שֶׁעָלְתָה.
phrases.english: the se'a that fell in is the se'a that came out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a משנה the גמרא started quoting just before this piece.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, the removed סאה is treated as the impure תרומה that fell in, so it must rot.

steps.title: The חכמים: The תרומה is nullified, but the mixture must be eaten carefully
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים hold that the תרומה is nullified in the hundred. They still require the mixture to be eaten in ways that avoid making it susceptible to טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: it is nullified. The mixture should be eaten dry or roasted, or kneaded with fruit juice, or divided into small doughs. The only condition is that no single place has an egg's volume [of the תרומה].
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the view of the חכמים. They disagree with רבי אליעזר and give practical ways to eat the mixture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, one in a hundred is nullified, so the whole mixture counts as חולין. The impure תרומה is still inside it, though, so they avoid wetting the food with water, since water makes food able to become טמא. Fruit juice does not have that effect. If someone does use water, he must keep each dough small enough that it holds less than an egg's volume of the תרומה. Less than a כביצה cannot pass on טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: It "rises", meaning it is nullified in the mixture
Eaten dry, in dry crumbled pieces
Fruit juice (it does not make food able to become טמא)
An egg's volume, the smallest amount of food that can become טמא

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: lift out one סאה and let it rot. The חכמים: the תרומה is nullified, but eat the mixture dry, roasted, with fruit juice, or in small doughs with less than a כביצה in each.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read "תעלה" as the same ruling as רבי אליעזר's "תירום ותרקב." For the חכמים, the תרומה is nullified (עולה) in the hundred, so nothing has to be left to rot.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: it is nullified,
and it is eaten dry, or roasted,
phrases.notes: The point is to keep water away from it, because water makes food able to become טמא.

phrases.english: or it is kneaded with fruit juice,
or it is divided into small doughs,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד כְּבֵיצָה.
phrases.english: provided that there is not an egg's volume in one place.
phrases.notes: He means an egg's volume of the תרומה inside any single dough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי אליעזר in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תרומה is nullified. The mixture is eaten in ways that prevent susceptibility to טומאה, with less than a כביצה of תרומה in any one place.

steps.title: Introducing a ברייתא that comments on this משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא taught about this משנה. It starts by speaking about those hundred סאה of חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught about it [in a ברייתא]: those חולין...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting to quote a ברייתא that adds to the משנה, and the rest of it comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "ותני עלה" tells us the coming source is a ברייתא attached to this exact משנה. Its subject is "those חולין," the hundred סאה of pure חולין the impure תרומה fell into. The new ruling about them comes right after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: "And it was taught about it": introduces a ברייתא on the משנה just quoted
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: And it was taught about it:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a ברייתא that comments on the משנה quoted in steps 1-2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduction only. The ברייתא's ruling about those חולין continues afterward.
